question: Which file wins when a submitter resends the same day?

plan.rationale: The question asks which file wins when a submitter resends on the same day, which is a general policy question covered by runbooks (latest-file-wins rule) and does not require data inspection.

summary: The resend with the later timestamp in the file name wins. Parse the `YYYYMMDD_HHMM` part of the name and order descending; the file with the highest `HHMM` for that business date is the one that supersedes earlier copies (and if timestamps tie, use the lexically greater name)【4】.

<context>
<passage id="1" source="incidents/INC-0438-mobile-column-rename.md" section="Fix">
INC-0438: MOBILE file renamed a dedup-key column | Fix
Submitter resent with the contracted header at 11:05 the same day. The day was reprocessed; the null-key rows were superseded by the resend under latest-file-wins.
</passage>

<passage id="2" source="runbooks/duplicate-submissions.md" section="Overview">
Duplicate submissions and the latest-file-wins rule | Overview
Submitters resend files. Sometimes it is a correction, sometimes an operator re-ran an export by mistake. Either way the same transaction lands twice and naive totals double count.
</passage>

<passage id="3" source="runbooks/submitter-onboarding.md" section="Resends">
Submitter files and naming convention | Resends
A resend uses the same date and a later `HHMM`. Submitters must not reuse a file name; the loader rejects a name it has already seen.
</passage>

<passage id="4" source="runbooks/duplicate-submissions.md" section="Which copy wins">
Duplicate submissions and the latest-file-wins rule | Which copy wins
The row from the **latest submitter file** wins. The file timestamp comes from the file name (`YYYYMMDD` business date, `HHMM` production time), not from load time, because files are sometimes loaded out of order during catch-up runs:  
```
SUBMITTERID_YYYYMMDD_HHMM_NAME.txt
S1002_20260612_1120_ECOMM.txt   <- wins over
S1002_20260612_0305_ECOMM.txt
```  
Parse `YYYYMMDD_HHMM` and order by it descending. If two files share the same timestamp (it has happened once), fall back to the lexically greater file name and raise it as an open question in the write-up.
</passage>

<passage id="5" source="runbooks/submitter-onboarding.md" section="Overview">
Submitter files and naming convention | Overview
Every submitter drops one pipe-delimited file per business day into the landing area. File names follow:  
```
SUBMITTERID_YYYYMMDD_HHMM_NAME.txt
```  
- `SUBMITTERID` is the id from `submitter_registry`, for example `S1001`.
- `YYYYMMDD` is the business date the file covers.
- `HHMM` is when the submitter produced the file, in UTC, on the morning after the business date. Together `YYYYMMDD_HHMM` decides which copy wins during dedup.
- `NAME` is the short submitter name, for example `POSFEED`.

| S1003 | MOBILE | mobile app | 03:30 |

</passage>
